summary: Frontend-only verification of Become-a-partner v2 form, PhoneAuthModal country selector, and Admin partner applicant-type badges + Site-settings T&C editor. All 8 acceptance items pass end-to-end EXCEPT one deviation on the strict India '10-digit cap' expectation (typing goes to ~13 national digits in the react-phone-number-input <input> because limitMaxLength doesn't hard-block extra keystrokes for IN; however submit stays disabled via isValidPhoneNumber gating, so functionally the flow is safe).

ui_bugs.issue: For India (+91), typing more than 10 digits is NOT hard-capped by react-phone-number-input's limitMaxLength — the raw input accepts up to ~13 national digits. Visual formatting stops updating past 10 digits but extra keystrokes still land in the value. isValidPhoneNumber correctly gates Submit, so no invalid submission occurs. Spec asked for a strict 10-digit cap.

acceptance_matrix.partner-phone India 10-digit hard cap: PARTIAL — extra digits still typable, but isValidPhoneNumber blocks submit
acceptance_matrix.applicant-type radios (Individual/LLP/Co: PASS (all 3 aria-checked=false initially; click flips to true)

action_items: MINOR: Consider enforcing a hard 10-digit numeric cap on PhoneField for defaultCountry=IN — react-phone-number-input's limitMaxLength does not fully prevent additional keystrokes past 10 national digits in this build (13 digits observed in raw input value). One-liner options: (a) also set maxLength on the internal <input> when country==='IN' (11 or 12 chars incl. space), or (b) sanitize onChange to strip beyond 10 national digits. Not a submission risk (isValidPhoneNumber currently blocks), so priority is low/cosmetic.

OPTIONAL: In Admin > Partner applications, older pending rows created before applicant_type existed have no badge. Either backfill with a default ('—' or 'Unknown') or hide the badge slot cleanly. Currently the badge slot just isn't rendered for those rows, which is acceptable.
critical_code_review_comments: BecomePartner.jsx submit path is clean and gating logic is correct; SEBI regex ^IN[A-Z][0-9]{9}$ matches the spec.
PhoneField wraps react-phone-number-input consistently for both public entry points (BecomePartner + PhoneAuthModal) — good DRY.
The partner-terms-modal content falls back to a placeholder when /api/content has no partnerTerms — handled gracefully.
AdminPage.jsx still very large; splitting Site-settings sub-blocks (footer, socials, partnerTerms) into components would help maintainability, but this iteration did not regress it.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (7.5/8 items fully pass; 10-digit hard cap partial)

seed_data_creation: Submitted one new partner application via UI (name: 'Test User FE', applicant_type: Company, unique IN mobile ~+91 98495 66600, SEBI INH000012345). Now visible in Admin > Partner applications with applicant_type='Company'.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 11 covered the full v2 Become-a-partner flow (phone selector, applicant-type radios, gating, T&C modal, submit success), PhoneAuthModal phone selector + OTP login (demo mode), and Admin applicant-type badges + Site-settings T&C editor persistence. Only outstanding gap is a soft (non-blocking) 10-digit cap on the phone input — main agent should decide whether to tighten it. All admin flows (Partner applications tab, Approved Partners tab with Anita Rao LLP badge, Site settings publish persists) verified working.
rca of the issue: 10-digit cap partial: react-phone-number-input's limitMaxLength depends on libphonenumber's parsing to stop accepting further digits; for India +91 it stops incrementing the FORMATTED national number past 10 digits, but the underlying controlled <input> still accepts additional keystrokes appended to the raw value string (observed input.value='+91 9876543210999' after typing 14 digits). Since form validity uses isValidPhoneNumber(E.164), the Submit button remains disabled — so user cannot submit an over-length number, but the UX allows the extra chars to remain visible. Fix suggestion: add an explicit onChange sanitizer or maxLength attribute to enforce the hard cap.
